A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MAST: Model-Agnostic Sparsified Training. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H report original logistic-regression experiments on a5a and a1a, including convergence trajectories and pruning accuracy distributions.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H report original logistic-regression, stochastic-gradient, distributed neural-network, and dropout-comparison results.

M1.justification: The MAST objective, Double Sketched (S)GD, distributed updates, L-SVRDSG, and S-PAGE procedures are retained. Perm-K is an experimental instantiation of the existing general sketch framework. Moving variance reduction from Section 4.2 to Appendix G does not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates logistic regression on a5a and a1a. V2 retains these datasets, adds w8a, and introduces distributed neural-network experiments using CIFAR-10-derived ResNet-50 embeddings and logit targets. ImageNet supplies pretrained weights rather than a separately reported evaluation.

E2.justification: V2 adds original, unscaled Dropout as a comparator in Figure 8 and a sketch-averaged stochastic-gradient control in Figure 5. ERM and exact GD remain in the pruning and Rand-1 comparisons, while v1's GD comparisons of validation and unsparsified test accuracy are removed.

E3.justification: The pruning comparison changes from validation-selected, 2000-iteration Rand-K training and 1000 sampled test masks to reported exact-gradient Perm-K optimization and evaluation of every partition mask. Its train/validation/test split changes from 70/18/12 to 75/25 train/test, with revised sparsity levels. New experiments introduce single-example data subsampling and a 10-client neural-network setup.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses separating data-sampling and sketch-sampling effects, neural-network learning-rate/sparsity sensitivity, and an ablation of dropout's 1/p scaling. It revises the pruning-robustness study and removes the earlier logistic-loss and validation trajectories. The existing Rand-1 step-size analysis is retained as Figure 6.

E5.justification: V1 Figure 1 reports five-run averages with shaded standard deviations; that figure and reporting are removed. V2 Appendix H.1 specifies ten randomly seeded partition realizations for its revised accuracy distributions. These different designs do not establish an increase from five to ten runs of the same experiment.

E6.justification: V2 replaces the pruning results under a different protocol, reporting narrower MAST accuracy distributions where v1 Figure 2b generally showed wider MAST dispersion. It adds w8a, data-subsampled SGD, and neural-network/dropout results, while removing v1 Figures 1 and 2a. V1 Figure 3 is retained as v2 Figure 6. The revised pruning results are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds Theorem 7 and its proof, bounding the MAST optimum without requiring strong convexity. Appendix D.2 changes erroneous equalities to inequalities in Theorem 9 and its derivation. The principal convergence results and most appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central claims about the MAST formulation, optimization properties, SGD variants, and distributed extensions. The added introductory contribution bullet foregrounds experimental validation already present in v1, without materially redefining these scientific claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes its scaled, unbiased sketches from original Dropout and explains the separate effects of data and sketch sampling. It removes v1's accuracy-based regularization discussion. Its new claim of consistently lower loss with unbiased Dropout overstates Figure 8: the p=0.9, gamma=0.05 panel favors biased Dropout.

D1.justification: V2 adds the Xeon Gold 6246 hardware specification, NumPy 1.26.2 array_split instructions for constructing partitions, and ResNet-50 feature/logit-label preparation details. The implementation link to Konstantin Mishchenko's repository is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds LeJeune et al. (2021) and references for ResNet, CIFAR-10, and NumPy, while removing several introductory loss-function and SGD references. Its positioning against compressed-model and dropout convergence research remains substantially intact. Publication updates to existing references do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the exposition: it shortens the introduction, moves and consolidates variance-reduction material in Appendix G, rewrites the experimental narrative, and divides Appendix H into focused analyses. Widespread language editing accompanies this restructuring.

P2.justification: V2 adopts conference formatting and substantially redesigns the figure presentation, replacing the earlier main-text panels and adding stochastic-gradient and neural-network plots. Figure 4 redisplays the pruning data as swarmplots, rather than adding another experiment. V1's Rand-1 Figure 3 is resized and retained as v2 Figure 6.

improvement.justification: V1's empirical validation is limited to single-node logistic regression with full-data gradients. V2 directly tests data-subsampled optimization, distributed neural-network behavior, and dropout scaling, substantially strengthening support for the framework's claimed scope. The added optimum bound and corrected inequalities also improve rigor. Some earlier uncertainty reporting disappears, and Figure 8 contradicts the claim of consistent unbiased-dropout superiority, but these limitations do not outweigh the broader, more targeted validation.
